html:
A long Ottoman blockade of Constantinople from 1394 to 1402, ordered by Sultan Bayezid I.

Bayezid had made the Byzantine emperor his vassal, but Manuel II would not obey him. The sultan cut the city off by land and built a fort on the Asian shore of the Bosporus to watch the sea. Food grew short and many people fled.

The West tried to help. A large crusade marched down the Danube, but Bayezid destroyed it at the Battle of Nicopolis in 1396. Manuel then left for Venice, Paris and London to beg for aid.

Rescue came from the east. Timur invaded Anatolia and crushed Bayezid at the Battle of Ankara in 1402, taking him prisoner. The siege ended, and the Ottoman state fell into a civil war among Bayezid's sons that bought Byzantium another half century.
sum: A long Ottoman blockade of Constantinople from 1394 to 1402, ordered by Sultan Bayezid I.
